arxiv-2505-06018.title: Black holes as gravitational mirrors

arxiv-2505-06018.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by L. C. N. Santos, F. M. da Silva, C. R. Muniz, V. B. Bezerra. Retrolensing is a gravitational lensing effect in which light emitted by a background source is deflected by a black hole and redirected toward the observer after undergoing nearly complete loops around the black hole. In this context, we explore the possibility of seeing objects of the solar system in past eras through telescope observations by using black holes as a gravitational mirror.

pmc-13671721.title: Notes from the Field: Dengue Outbreak — U.S. Virgin Islands, January 2024–June 2025
pmc-13671721.creator: Sarah Gallalee, Hannah M. Cranford, Andra Prosper, Annellie Gumbs, Valerie V. Mac, Jendai Richards, Aubrey Drummond, Laura E. Adams, Gilberto A. Santiago, Parker K. Acevedo, Marlon Lawrence, Lisa LaPlace Ekpo, Brett R. Ellis, Esther M. Ellis
pmc-13671721.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). During 2024–2025, the U.S. Virgin Islands (USVI) experienced its first dengue virus outbreak in approximately a decade, including 263 confirmed cases and the territory’s first confirmed dengue virus–associated death since 2005. The outbreak response included implementing diagnostic testing for dengue in USVI for the first time, clinical trainings on case management and testing, deployment of a web-based electronic reporting platform, territorywide vector control campaigns, and community outreach and education. What are the implications for public health practice?
